code_quality.title: Extract reusable PlatformStudio component to eliminate 6 duplicate studio files
code_quality.description: The 6 platform studio files (LinkedInStudio.tsx, YouTubeStudio.tsx, InstagramStudio.tsx, FacebookStudio.tsx, TikTokStudio.tsx, XStudio.tsx) are nearly identical. Each file is ~86 lines with the only difference being the platform config key. This is textbook code duplication that violates DRY principles and makes maintenance difficult - any change must be applied 6 times.
code_quality.rationale: Code duplication is one of the highest-impact code smells. These 516 lines (6 × 86) can be reduced to ~100 lines with a single generic PlatformStudio component. This eliminates the risk of inconsistency, reduces merge conflicts, and simplifies testing since only one component needs coverage.
code_quality.currentState: 6 nearly identical files, each defining the same interface (StudioProps), same component structure, same hooks usage, differing only in PLATFORM_CONFIGS key
code_quality.proposedChange: Create a single generic PlatformStudio component that accepts platform as a prop. Replace all 6 files with a simple re-export pattern or inline usage: <PlatformStudio platform='linkedin' {...props} />
code_quality.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - When multiple pieces of code do the same thing, extract to a single source of truth

code_quality.title: Split App.tsx (935 lines) into focused modules using feature-based organization
code_quality.description: App.tsx has grown to 935 lines and handles too many concerns: routing (AdminRouter), voice agent wrapper, keyboard shortcuts configuration, navigation state, generation state, refresh logic, onboarding, and modal management. This 'God component' pattern makes the file difficult to understand, test, and maintain.
code_quality.rationale: Large root components are a major source of bugs and developer frustration. They create high cognitive load during code reviews, make it difficult to isolate test scenarios, and increase the blast radius of changes. Breaking this into focused modules improves separation of concerns and enables parallel development.
code_quality.currentState: Single 935-line file with AppContent (700+ lines), AdminRouter (70 lines), AdminLoadingFallback, VoiceAgentWrapper, and App function all in one file
code_quality.proposedChange: Split into: (1) src/routes/AdminRouter.tsx - admin routing logic, (2) src/routes/AppRouter.tsx - main app routing, (3) src/providers/VoiceAgentWrapper.tsx - voice context bridge, (4) src/hooks/useStudioState.ts - studio state management, (5) src/hooks/useAppShortcuts.ts - keyboard shortcuts configuration. App.tsx becomes ~100 lines of composition.
code_quality.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change
prerequisites: Ensure test coverage for keyboard shortcuts and voice integration before refactoring

code_quality.title: Split database schema.ts (578 lines) into domain-based modules
code_quality.description: The server's schema.ts file contains 36 database tables (578 lines) in a single file spanning multiple domains: authentication, profiles, teams, chat, images, admin, agents, billing, and observability. This makes it difficult to navigate, understand relationships, and maintain domain boundaries.
code_quality.rationale: Monolithic schema files violate separation of concerns and make it harder to reason about data models. Splitting by domain enables better encapsulation, clearer ownership, easier code review, and aligns with the planned feature co-location strategy mentioned in CLAUDE.md.
code_quality.currentState: Single 578-line file with 36 tables covering 9+ domains with inline section comments as the only organization
code_quality.proposedChange: Split into domain modules: server/src/db/schema/auth.ts (users, sessions, tokens), server/src/db/schema/profiles.ts (profiles, preferences, apiKeys), server/src/db/schema/teams.ts (teams, members, brands), server/src/db/schema/chat.ts (conversations, messages, transcripts), server/src/db/schema/gallery.ts (images, designs), server/src/db/schema/admin.ts (adminUsers, audit, rateLimit), server/src/db/schema/agents.ts (configs, skills, mcp), server/src/db/schema/billing.ts (tiers, credits, transactions), server/src/db/schema/observability.ts (traces, metrics, logs). Create server/src/db/schema/index.ts barrel export.
code_quality.bestPractice: Domain-Driven Design - organize code around business domains, not technical layers
prerequisites: Ensure all Drizzle queries use explicit imports to avoid circular dependencies

code_quality.title: Reduce eslint-disable directives (40 occurrences) through proper typing and refactoring
code_quality.description: There are 40 eslint-disable comments across 28 files, indicating systematic bypassing of linting rules. The most common disables are for @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any and unused variables. This technical debt accumulates silently and undermines the value of having strict TypeScript configuration.
code_quality.rationale: ESLint rules exist to prevent bugs and maintain code quality. Disabling them should be exceptional, not routine. High eslint-disable counts indicate either: (1) rules that don't fit the project (should be adjusted in config), or (2) code that needs refactoring to meet standards. Addressing this reduces runtime errors and improves IDE support.
code_quality.currentState: 40 eslint-disable comments across 28 files, with AIContext.tsx having 3, ImageGallery.tsx having 4, and ExportPanel.tsx having 4. Many are disabling 'no-explicit-any' and 'no-unused-vars'.
code_quality.proposedChange: Audit each eslint-disable: (1) For 'no-explicit-any' - add proper TypeScript generics or interface definitions, (2) For 'no-unused-vars' - remove unused code or use underscore prefix convention, (3) For legitimate exceptions - add inline explanation comment. Target: reduce from 40 to <10 necessary exceptions.
code_quality.bestPractice: TypeScript strictness - leverage the type system for safety; eslint-disable should be rare and documented

code_quality.title: Extract SettingsModal sections (631 lines) into focused sub-components
code_quality.description: SettingsModal.tsx has grown to 631 lines handling multiple concerns: API key management for 3 providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Replicate), model selection dropdowns for 4 model types, connection testing UI, session timeout configuration, and save/validation logic. The component is difficult to test in isolation and changes to one section risk affecting others.
code_quality.rationale: Large modal components are particularly problematic because they often contain complex state management and validation logic that becomes intertwined. Breaking this into sub-components enables focused unit tests, reduces cognitive load, and enables reuse (e.g., APIKeyInput could be used in onboarding).
code_quality.currentState: Single 631-line component with inline ConnectionStatus component, 3 API key sections with similar structure, 4 model dropdown sections with similar structure, and mixed concerns
code_quality.proposedChange: Extract into focused components: (1) src/components/features/settings/APIKeySection.tsx - reusable API key input with test button and status, (2) src/components/features/settings/ModelSelector.tsx - dropdown with model list and description, (3) src/components/features/settings/ConnectionStatus.tsx - extracted and properly typed, (4) src/components/features/settings/useSettingsForm.ts - custom hook for form state and validation. SettingsModal becomes ~150 lines of composition.
code_quality.bestPractice: Component composition - build complex UIs from simple, focused, reusable components
